claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys can be used as low-activation structural materials for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
Refractory high-entropy alloys have excellent high-temperature mechanical properties.
Refractory high-entropy alloys have irradiation resistance suitable for fusion-reactor applications.
Fusion-reactor environments relevant to plasma-facing components involve high temperatures and high radiation levels.
Refractory high-entropy alloys maintain microstructural stability under extreme fusion-reactor conditions.
The composition and microstructure of refractory high-entropy alloys allow them to maintain mechanical integrity under fusion-reactor conditions.
The composition and microstructure of refractory high-entropy alloys enable resistance to degradation under fusion-reactor conditions.
Using refractory high-entropy alloys would improve the performance of plasma-facing components.
Using refractory high-entropy alloys would increase the longevity of plasma-facing components.
Current plasma-facing-component materials may withstand extreme fusion-reactor conditions less effectively than refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed application of refractory high-entropy alloys is limited to high-temperature, high-radiation fusion-reactor environments.
Specific performance metrics for refractory high-entropy alloys under fusion-reactor conditions are not fully characterized.
